planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix; Blue Curls echeveria holds its powdery blue color and tight rosette form best in bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix; Blue Curls echeveria holds its powdery blue color and tight rosette form best in bright light. Thick, powdery, silvery-blue leaves curl gently backward at the tips, forming a loose, spreading rosette that offsets readily to form small clusters, and the popular 'Topsy Turvy' selection of this species curls its leaves even more dramatically. Native to dry hillsides in northeastern Mexico, it is easy to grow and propagate, tolerating a range of light conditions though coloring and form are best in bright light, making it a versatile addition to a succulent dish garden or xeriscape container arrangement. Water only when the soil is fully dry, avoid wetting the leaves to protect the delicate powdery bloom, and separate offsets to propagate.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Plush Plant flowers reliably with bright light and needs excellent drainage to avoid rot.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Plush Plant flowers reliably with bright light and needs excellent drainage to avoid rot. Thick, softly fuzzy, velvety green leaves edged in red give this shrubby Mexican succulent an appealingly plush, tactile texture unlike the smoother, glossier leaves of most other echeveria species, topped by clusters of vivid orange-red, bell-shaped flowers that resemble tiny firecrackers, giving the plant its alternate common name. Its upright, branching, shrub-like habit sets it apart from the flatter rosette form typical of most echeverias, making it a good textural and structural accent in a succulent container arrangement. Water only when the soil is fully dry, provide bright light for compact growth and reliable flowering, and propagate easily from stem cuttings.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Mexican Hens holds its ruffled leaf form and frosty color best in bright light with cooler nights.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Mexican Hens holds its ruffled leaf form and frosty color best in bright light with cooler nights. Thin, wavy, deeply ruffled leaves coated in a fine, frosty, powdery bloom form an elegant, undulating rosette in shades of soft pink, lavender, and gray, one of the most delicately textured and colorful echeveria species commonly grown, with color intensifying in cooler weather and bright light. Native to rocky slopes in Mexico, it offsets to form small clusters over time and is a favorite for succulent arrangements and collector displays for its uniquely ruffled, almost paper-thin leaf texture. Water only when the soil is fully dry, avoid wetting the leaves to protect the delicate powdery coating, and provide bright light for the best ruffling and color.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Golden Sedum colors most vividly gold in bright light and stays greener in shade.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Golden Sedum colors most vividly gold in bright light and stays greener in shade. Thick, glossy, translucent-edged leaves are packed densely along upright then trailing stems, coloring a warm golden-yellow with rosy-red tips in bright light, an eye-catching color shift from the pale green of lower-light conditions that makes this Mexican sedum popular for its responsive, sun-loving coloring. Its stems eventually trail and cascade as they lengthen, making it useful for a hanging basket or the edge of a mixed succulent container where its warm coloring can spill over an edge. Water only when the soil is fully dry, provide bright direct light for the best golden color, and propagate easily from stem or leaf cuttings.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Clubbed Sedum forms tight, dense rosettes and rots quickly in wet or dense soil.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Clubbed Sedum forms tight, dense rosettes and rots quickly in wet or dense soil. Thick, club-shaped, powdery blue-gray leaves are densely packed into tight, compact rosettes that offset readily to form a spreading mat, blushing soft pink at the tips in bright light and producing small white star-shaped flowers on short stalks in spring. Native to rocky slopes in Mexico, it forms an unusually neat, symmetrical rosette compared to many trailing sedums, making it a favorite for succulent arrangements and rock garden pockets where its tidy form can be appreciated. Water only when the soil is fully dry, avoid wetting the leaves to protect the powdery coating, and provide bright light for the tightest, best-colored rosettes.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Jelly Bean Plant develops its best red tips in bright light and stays plain green in shade.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Jelly Bean Plant develops its best red tips in bright light and stays plain green in shade. Plump, cylindrical, blue-green leaves tipped in bright coral-red closely resemble a cluster of jelly beans, an appropriately whimsical common name for this easy, fast-growing Mexican sedum that branches and spreads readily along sprawling stems, eventually forming a substantial mound or trailing mass in a container or garden bed. One of the most widely grown and easily propagated sedums, it roots readily from stem or leaf cuttings and tolerates a range of conditions, making it a popular, low-maintenance choice for succulent arrangements and xeriscape plantings alike. Water only when the soil is fully dry, provide bright light for the best red coloring, and propagate easily from cuttings.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Miniature Pine Tree needs excellent drainage and benefits from pruning to maintain a shrubby, well-branched shape.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Miniature Pine Tree needs excellent drainage and benefits from pruning to maintain a shrubby, well-branched shape. Narrow, needle-like, evenly spaced leaves clothe upright, woody-based stems in a whorled pattern that closely mimics the look of a miniature conifer branch, an unusual and distinctive texture among succulents that has made this South African species a favorite for succulent bonsai and novelty container displays. Its shrubby, self-branching habit and slow, tree-like growth over years make it a good long-term specimen for a sunny windowsill or patio container, developing thicker, more tree-like stems as it matures. Water only when the soil is fully dry, provide bright light for compact growth, and prune to encourage a fuller, more branched, tree-like shape.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Lavender Scallops spreads readily by both stem growth and plantlets that form along leaf edges.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Lavender Scallops spreads readily by both stem growth and plantlets that form along leaf edges. Rounded, scalloped, blue-gray leaves are edged in a distinct purple-pink margin that deepens in bright light, and like other kalanchoe relatives in this group, small plantlets sometimes form along the notched leaf edges and drop to root nearby, helping the plant spread and multiply readily in a garden bed or container. Its easy, fast growth and attractive two-tone leaf color make it a popular, low-maintenance succulent for a sunny border or xeriscape container in frost-free climates, and it roots easily from stem or leaf cuttings for further propagation. Water only when the soil is fully dry, provide bright light for the best leaf color, and protect from frost outside the warmest zones.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference
